app/next.config.mjs:7-10 — only config option is turbopack.root, stable since the top-level `turbopack` key (Next 15.3+; Turbopack is the stable default bundler in Next 16)
app/app/page.jsx:9 — `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, a stable route segment config since 13.4
app/components/HomeControls.jsx:3-4 — useRouter/usePathname, stable next/navigation hooks since 13.4

reach.rationale: The app relies exclusively on long-stable APIs on the current stable LTS release; there is nothing experimental or even recently-stable at its core.

evidence: app/next.config.mjs:1-10 — the single framework-config touchpoint is 10 lines, isolated and documented
grep across app/ (excluding .next/) — zero unstable_/experimental_ names, no flags, no canary dependencies
containment.rationale: There is nothing to contain: no experimental APIs or flags appear anywhere in the source, and the one config option used is stable and confined to next.config.mjs.

evidence: app/app/page.jsx:9 — force-dynamic + app/lib/api.js:14 fetch with cache:'no-store' directly satisfy the spec's 'fetch at request time' rule rather than reaching for newer caching APIs
app/components/PokemonCard.jsx:16-19 — plain for sprites instead of next/image, a conservative stable choice

justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, and where the framework offered newer options (cacheComponents/use cache, next/image) the app deliberately chose the boring stable path that still meets the spec.

findings.issue: `dynamic = 'force-dynamic'` is duplicated on every route and is the pre-Next-16 caching escape hatch; it works fine today but is the legacy model as the framework moves to Cache Components.
findings.suggestion: Fine to keep for this spec (data must be live); consider documenting per-route why it's set, or revisit when migrating to the cacheComponents model in a future major.

summary: The app is maximally conservative: it targets the exact current stable LTS (next 16.4.3, react 19.2) and uses only long-stable App Router APIs, with no experimental flags, unstable_ imports, or canary dependencies. Its one non-trivial config (turbopack.root) is a stable, documented option confined to next.config.mjs. As a codebase to own, this carries essentially zero framework-version risk.
